title: Quant Fidelity Oracle and Experimental Scheduler for Regression Detection & Threshold Tuning
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a reproducible, production-friendly evaluation harness (the "Quant Fidelity Oracle") plus an experimental scheduler that runs controlled AWQ/GPTQ quantization variants (int8/int4 and mixed) across targeted holdout cohorts and configuration deltas. The Oracle must: 1) surface quality regressions tied to quant profiles and config changes, 2) synthesize per-model/profile threshold recommendations (rollback/canary gates), and 3) emit structured signals for Console dashboards and automated runbooks.

Motivation: Current quant-eval tickets run ad-hoc sweeps and produce artifacts that are hard to compare across releases, cohorts, and metrics. We need a single canonical runner that standardizes datasets, metrics, tolerances, and the threshold-sweeper algorithm so engineering and PMs can make deterministic rollout decisions for quant profiles.

Scope: Implement evaluation pipeline (runner + metric collectors), a threshold-sweeper engine (grid + adaptive search), analysis notebooks, and integration points for Console alerts + GitHub PR checks. Initially support AWQ and GPTQ paths for int8/int4; later extend to mixed-precision and per-layer presets.
acceptance_criteria: Oracle runs a reproducible batch comparing fp16 reference vs AWQ/GPTQ int8 and int4 variants for a given model and dataset in under 4h for our medium-sized suite (1000 prompts).
Threshold-sweeper proposes a per-model profile threshold (semantic-similarity delta and exact-match delta) with a suggested rollback probability and confidence score.
Automated report includes: per-cohort metric table, latency and throughput delta, and a single recommended action: PASS / WARNING / FAIL.
Integration: Oracle publishes results to Console dataset (CSV + JSON manifest) and creates a draft PR comment template with a short summary and link to artifacts.
End-to-end tests: CI job runs a tiny synthetic sweep that asserts metric calculations and that thresholds are computed deterministically.
plan: Week 1: Design data model + metric definitions; pick canonical holdout cohorts (general, high-precision, safety-sensitive).
Week 2: Implement runner for AWQ and GPTQ variants; hook up tokenized latency recorder and golden fp16 baselines.
Week 3: Build threshold-sweeper (initial grid search + Bayesian/ASHA fallback) and produce recommendation logic.
Week 4: Console integration (artifact uploader) + CI integration + docs and runbook for SRE/Release engineers.
Post-release: Expand to mixed-precision and include per-layer annealing options; add automated alerts in Console with rollback playbook.
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with PM and Design — agreed canonical cohorts: general (wikiQA-style), high-precision (SQuAD-style), and hallucination-sensitive (LLM safety prompts).
2026-03-04: Implemented baseline fp16 runner and dataset loader; pushed initial harness to feature/quant-oracle. PR #2897 opened for early feedback (see artifacts).
2026-03-07: Ran first AWQ int8 sweep on small cohort (200 prompts). Observed semantic-similarity drop concentrated in long-answer prompts; added 'answer-length' cohort split to plan.
2026-03-10: Design review — PM asked for confidence-scoring on threshold suggestions; agreed to add bootstrap sampling to compute variance for recommendation confidence.
2026-03-12: Integrated latency/throughput recorder; initial results show int8 AWQ reduces p99 token latency by ~18% but increases hallucination-rate metric by 1.2% on the safety cohort.

2026-03-14: Added adaptive sweeper prototype (Bayesian optimization seed + fallback grid). Preparing CI synthetic test and Console upload flow. Blocker: storage quota for full-suite runs in staging cluster (ticket to infra needed).
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives from small cohorts leading to unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: require minimum sample sizes and bootstrap confidence intervals before issuing FAIL status.
Risk: AWQ/GPTQ toolchain variance producing non-deterministic artifacts. Mitigation: pin quant toolchain versions and snapshot model weights; record toolchain metadata in artifact manifest.
Risk: Long runtime for full sweep. Mitigation: experimental scheduler supports staged runs (smoke -> subset -> full) and early stopping if metrics are clearly within tolerances.
Risk: Console alert fatigue. Mitigation: only emit WARN/FAIL when both quality delta and customer-impacting metric exceed thresholds; include rollback playbook link in alert.
metrics: Primary quality metrics: semantic-similarity (BERTScore variant), exact-match, answer-length drift, hallucination-rate (heuristic), token-level perplexity delta.
Performance metrics: median and p99 token latency, throughput (tokens/sec), memory usage delta.
Operational metrics: run-time hours per sweep, flake-rate (failed runs), artifact size (MB).
Decision metrics: recommendation confidence (0-1), suggested action (PASS/WARN/FAIL) and rollback probability estimate.
rollout_plan: Alpha: Internal runs on staging with human review; dashboards link in #infra-quant channel. Goal: 2 full-model runs across cohorts with actionable reports.
Beta: Wire results into Console as opt-in alerting for a set of pilot teams (eng + two customers). Capture feedback on thresholds and metrics.
GA: Default integration into release gating pipeline; threshold recommendations can be used by canary/rollback automation when confidence > 0.8.
Post-GA: Add mixed-precision sweeps and tie into Optimize recommendations for auto-tuning quant profiles.
